caption:
Night on the ground, day in the air. These are the highest clouds.

Sunset reaches the high air last. Clouds up there still catch sunlight.
Water vapour freezes into these clouds. It needs very cold air in summer, far north.
This NASA photo was taken from the space station, 267 miles up.

What the astronomers say: most of what we know about these clouds was found in the past twenty years, and how they form is still being studied.

NASA picture: JSC, iss074e0796136. Credit: NASA/Chris Williams
